query: What is the current national norovirus category on the WastewaterSCAN dashboard as of today (High/Medium/Low), and is it rising, falling, or stable? Note the unusual summer 2026 GII.17 off-season surge.
answer:
## Summary

**Current national norovirus category on WastewaterSCAN: MEDIUM, trending down/falling** — per the most recent official newsletter (June 2026 update, through June 30, 2026). Median GII concentrations fell ~37% from May to June, reflecting the normal post-winter seasonal decline. GII was still detected in 99% of samples.

**But there's an important "as of today" nuance:** Independent surveillance reporting describes an **unusual summer 2026 off-season surge** building in July — after the June newsletter's cutoff — with ≥12 states elevated (Utah, Texas, Ohio, North Carolina, Pennsylvania leading), driven by cruise-ship outbreaks, camp/restaurant exposures, and contaminated shellfish. So the two signals are in tension: the last *official* national categorical read was MEDIUM/falling (end-June), while real-time July signals point to renewed, geographically concentrated rising activity.

**The GII.17 connection:** This off-season behavior is tied to GII.17 displacing GII.4 as the dominant genotype (GII.17 outbreak share rose 7.5% → 34.3% → 75.4% across the last three seasons, while GII.4 collapsed to 10.7%). Because GII.4 historically drove the sharp winter-peak seasonality, its decline plus GII.17 dominance has produced less predictable seasonality and prolonged summer circulation — exactly the dynamic behind the summer 2026 surge.

**Key caveats:** WastewaterSCAN had not yet posted a July 2026 newsletter at research time, so the exact mid-July national category couldn't be directly confirmed. Also, the widely-cited NBC "HIGH/rising" figure is from **May 2025** (prior season), not the current period.
